study: Speckesser et al. 2018 — EEF Embedding Formative Assessment (EFA) effectiveness trial
eval_evidence: EEF-commissioned effectiveness trial; independent evaluation team (NIESR/UCL — Speckesser, Runge, Foliano, Anders et al.), separate from the program originators (Wiliam/Leahy) and the delivery body.
developer_evidence: PD was delivered by SSAT (the Schools, Students and Teachers network), 'an independent membership organisation', which supplied resource packs and Lead Practitioner support — not the original developers; schools then ran their own monthly Teacher Learning Communities (TLCs).
cascade_evidence: Train-the-trainer/lead-teacher cascade: 'Each school appointed a lead teacher who attended an initial training day and received ongoing implementation support from an SSAT Lead Practitioner'; the lead teacher then ran the monthly TLC workshops for the rest of the staff (>=1 extra hop).
counterfactual_evidence: Two-arm effectiveness trial vs a business-as-usual control group; control schools continued normal practice (no EFA resource pack/TLCs).
coaching_evidence: No external in-class coaching; the in-school mechanism is monthly 75-90 min TLC workshops plus teacher-to-teacher peer lesson observation between sessions — workshop/peer-based, not recurring expert in-class coaching cycles.
student_dose_evidence: A whole-staff formative-assessment professional-development program (TLCs); only the teachers' regular instruction changes — no tutoring or added student-facing dose.
maturity_evidence: Effectiveness trial in schools new to EFA; the 18 monthly TLCs ran over the trial period and GCSE outcomes were measured at the end of that single implementation rollout (teachers new to the program).
